candidate.fires_on: dd3y (or dd52) exceeds the screen threshold WHILE pct_off_low > 0.40; require both anchors before enqueueing. Additionally void the setup when the peak defining the drawdown printed at a valuation multiple >2x the current one (normalization, not compression).
candidate.evidence_here: AVPT: dd3y 35.0% admitted it, but the pack shows dd52 -21.3% with pct_off_low +49.3%, and the $19.99 peak was ~10x EV/S vs 5.1x today. The screen bought a corrected multiple, half-corrected back.

candidate.name: distributor_contract_asset_impairment_cliff
candidate.one_line: Issuer capitalizes a large upfront payment to its own distributor as a multi-decade contract asset amortized against revenue, so a single counterparty simultaneously controls revenue, a senior mezzanine claim, and a balance-sheet asset larger than tangible common equity.
candidate.fires_on: A contract asset >10% of total assets, or > (total common equity minus goodwill), whose counterparty is also (a) >25% of revenue, (b) a holder of preferred/mezzanine paper, or (c) the subject of disclosed securities litigation over that same agreement. Amortization term >10 years is an aggravator: it defers the cost recognition well past the agreement's renewal risk.
candidate.evidence_here: CELH 10-Q 6/30/26: $598.8M Pepsi contract asset amortized as contra-revenue over ~17 years; goodwill $919.7M; total common equity $1,199.6M (contract asset + goodwill = $1,518.5M > equity, before Alani/Rockstar brand intangibles). Same counterparty holds $1,760.0M of Series A/B mezzanine (liquidation preference $1,135M) and ~59% of revenue, and is the subject of a consolidated securities class action plus five derivative actions alleging misstatements about that distribution agreement.

candidate.name: guidance_step_up_arithmetic_gate
candidate.one_line: Compute required H2 (or remaining-period) result as FY guide minus reported YTD actual, expressed as % over the reported period; fire when the implied step-up exceeds 30% with no disclosed bridge.
candidate.fires_on: FY guide reaffirmed/raised on the TOP line while the PROFIT line is cut, and (FYguide_low - YTD_actual) / YTD_actual > 0.30, and the release provides no quantified bridge (cost actions, backlog, price realization) and no cash-flow guidance
candidate.evidence_here: TNC H1'26 adj EBITDA $64.4M vs FY26 guide $155-170M => required H2 $90.6-105.6M = +40.7% to +64.0% over H1, while the H1 run-rate was -30.0% YoY; 8-K Ex-99.1 2026-08-05 gave no bridge and no FY cash-flow outlook. Both benches valued the name off the guide midpoint without ever computing the stub.

candidate.name: fx_translated_guidance_raise_masking_organic_decline
candidate.one_line: A FY revenue-guidance RAISE driven wholly by FX translation and tuck-in M&A while organic growth is negative in every region — and the same release cuts the margin guide, because the translated revenue carries the weakest-margin geography.
candidate.fires_on: reported revenue growth > 0 AND organic growth < 0 across all disclosed regions AND FY revenue guide raised AND FY EBITDA/EPS guide cut in the same document; screens keyed on fwd_rev_growth_pct rank the issuer UP on the raise
candidate.evidence_here: TNC H1'26: reported +$13.3M (+2.2%) = FX +$16.9M + acquisitions +$3.5M on organic -$7.0M (-1.15%); Americas -0.7%, EMEA -1.0%, APAC -6.8% organic. Revenue guide raised to $1.270-1.310B, adj EBITDA guide cut to $155-170M in the same 8-K. The desk screen scored the raise and the blue brief adopted 'volume recovered, only margin is broken' verbatim.

candidate.name: deferred_tax_asset_inflated_equity_depresses_screen_roe

candidate.fires_on: DTA >= 15% of total assets AND DTA >= 25% of total stockholders' equity AND ROE_ex_DTA_equity >= 1.7x reported ROE; escalate if the DTA is declining while 'deferred taxes' is a positive add-back to OCF (reported FCF is being subsidized by the asset's consumption).
candidate.evidence_here: ALGN 10-Q 2026-06-30: DTA $1,479,864K = 23.1% of $6,417,581K total assets and 35.0% of $4,232,453K equity; equity ex-DTA/goodwill/intangibles $2,160M implies ROE ~19-20% vs the screen's 10.2%. candidate.name: activist_commitment_vs_realized_buyback_gap

candidate.fires_on: 8-K/PR announces an increased annual repurchase target following activist engagement AND the most recent 10-Q shows YTD repurchases below 50% of the prior-year same-period figure AND the residual required H2 spend exceeds 2.5x the realized H1 pace.

Secondary coverage and the sponsoring brief both read the announcement as an increase in capital return.

candidate.name: book_to_bill_vs_organic_revenue_divergence
candidate.one_line: When disclosed ORDERS grow while organic REVENUE declines (book-to-bill >1.0 with rising backlog), the revenue line is measuring a fulfillment constraint, not demand — and any bench that reads only the revenue/geographic table will mis-diagnose a timing problem as terminal demand loss.
candidate.fires_on: issuer discloses orders and/or backlog separately from revenue; orders YoY > 0 AND organic revenue YoY < 0 AND backlog rising AND a named internal fulfillment disruption (ERP cutover, plant move, supply constraint) is disclosed in the same document
candidate.evidence_here: TNC Q2'26: orders $339.5M +6.6% YoY, backlog $127M, revenue $324.0M => book-to-bill 1.05, against organic revenue -1.15% H1 and negative organic in all three regions. RED built its FATAL finding 2 ('a business whose units are shrinking') entirely off the geographic organic table and never read the orders line; BLUE-1 never pulled it either. The same 8-K guides FY organic +3.5-7.0%, which is only coherent given the backlog.

candidate.name: covenant_restriction_severity_misread_cap_as_prohibition

candidate.fires_on: a bench cites a leverage-triggered dividend/buyback restriction as a kill or sizing constraint WITHOUT quoting the basket size, and the issuer's actual annual distribution is materially below that basket
candidate.evidence_here: TNC 2024 Credit Agreement: above 2.50x leverage, payments are 'limited to 10% of consolidated total assets and $100.0 million during any fiscal year.' RED's finding 6 concluded 'two more Q2-shaped quarters put the 54-year dividend streak inside the restricted zone.' TNC's annual dividend is ~$21M against a $100M basket — the streak is unthreatened even at 3.7x. The covenant binds discretionary buybacks only, which had already stopped (Q2 repurchases: 5,515 shares, tax-withholding and swap only).

candidate.name: reported_growth_multiple_fx_inflation

candidate.fires_on: Issuer discloses both reported and FX-adjusted growth for ARR/revenue AND (reported - FX-adjusted) >= 2pts AND non-domestic revenue share > 50% per the geography footnote; re-state the growth rate used in every multiple comparison to the FX-adjusted figure and re-rank.
candidate.evidence_here: AVPT: ARR +27% reported vs +24% FX-adjusted (8-K EX-99.1); 10-Q geography shows North America $48.7M of $124.5M Q2 revenue = 39%. Both benches priced 5.1x EV/S against a 22-27% grower; the constant-currency grower is ~19-20% on revenue, which converts 'cheap-ish' to 'fair-to-full' without any other change.

candidate.name: gross_retention_mix_headwind_false_leak

candidate.name: index_boundary_gate_beta_contamination

candidate.name: extractive_cash_cost_margin_incommensurable

candidate.name: beat_and_cut_guidance_divergence

candidate.name: imported_seasonality_base_effect

candidate.name: shipment_vs_scanner_load_unwind

Consequence: any re-court trigger set on the lapping quarter's reported YoY is uninterpretable — move resolution one quarter later or require a scanner/depletion disclosure.
candidate.evidence_here: CELH Q3'25 PR: CELSIUS-brand revenue +44% YoY vs 13% U.S. scanner growth = 31pt gap; Q3'25 flagship ~$382M. candidate.name: internal_management_fee_capitalization

candidate.evidence_here: KTcs (058850, 0.39x book, W2,190 vs BVPS W5,640) and KTis (058860, KT stake 29.3%) are twin regional captives of KT with a repeatedly-floated AICC merger; Korean merger-ratio statute prices off market VWAP, so consolidation would exchange KTcs minorities at ~W2,190 and extinguish the W3,450/sh book gap rather than close it.

candidate.name: acquisition_annualisation_lap_date
candidate.one_line: Before ruling a segment's growth an acquisition artifact, compute the lap date from the deal completion dates — an annualisation step that has already fully lapped makes the NEXT period's comp clean and the growth gate genuinely discriminating.
candidate.fires_on: A bench dismisses a segment growth rate as 'includes annualisation of prior-year acquisitions' AND the acquisitions completed >12 months before the START of the period being courted.
candidate.evidence_here: CARD.L: red voided the >=15% HY27 partnerships gate as annualisation-contaminated, but Garlanna (4-Sep-2024) and Garven (4-Dec-2024) both closed in H2 FY25, so HY26's GBP6.6m->GBP16.5m carried the entire step and HY27-vs-HY26 is organic. The gate red called undiscriminating is the court's cleanest falsifier.

candidate.name: statutory_treasury_cancellation_clock
candidate.one_line: A statutory amendment forcing cancellation-or-shareholder-approved-retention of legacy treasury stock converts a dormant treasury block into a dated, zero-cash per-share accretion event with a legal deadline.
candidate.fires_on: Jurisdiction enacts mandatory treasury-share cancellation with a transition window for pre-existing holdings; issuer carries treasury >5% of outstanding; issuer trades below book so cancellation is book-accretive; deadline is disclosable and dated.
candidate.evidence_here: Korea's amended Commercial Act effective 2026-03-06 requires treasury held before that date to be cancelled or covered by an annually shareholder-approved retention plan by ~2027-09-06; KTcs cancelled 1,280,550 shares on 2026-03-31 citing the amendment and still holds 3,465,721 (9.1% of 37.94M outstanding) at 0.37x book.

candidate.name: vwap_merger_crystallization_requires_asymmetric_valuation
candidate.one_line: Guard on red's statutory_merger_price_crystallization: a market-VWAP intra-group merger only crystallizes a minority's book discount when the COUNTERPARTY is valued off book/appraisal; between two similarly-discounted listed entities the exchange ratio is discount-neutral and no loss is realized.
candidate.fires_on: Proposed intra-group merger where BOTH legs are listed and both trade at comparable price/book; ratio set by statutory market formula; appraisal rights also market-referenced.
candidate.evidence_here: KTcs (0.37x book) and KTis (P/E 4.29, yield 5.51%, cap W76.7B) are both KOSPI-listed KT captives at comparable discounts, and KTis already owns 11.97% of KTcs — a VWAP exchange preserves the discount in the survivor rather than realizing it, refuting the FATAL tag red attached.

candidate.name: pre_post_soc_intensification_confound
candidate.one_line: A within-patient pre/post efficacy delta in a chronic-progression disease is confounded by standard-of-care intensification that occurs at trial entry, so the headline effect cannot transfer to a concurrently-controlled Phase 3.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer markets a pre/post (within-patient) slope or progression-rate improvement as evidence for a randomized, concurrently-controlled pivotal, AND (a) the pre period predates trial-entry SoC optimization, or (b) arms randomized 1:1 show a larger BASELINE-period spread than POST-period spread (post-convergence across dose levels).
candidate.evidence_here: PROK REGEN-007: randomized G1 (n=24) and G2 (n=25) show pre-slopes -5.8 vs -3.4 (spread 2.4) but post-slopes -1.3 vs -1.7 (spread 0.4). The full-dose-vs-half-dose 'dose response' lives entirely in the pre period, at 6x the post-period separation. FDA's accelerated-approval agreement independently conditions the >=1.5 bar on 'versus sham controls' 'receiving appropriate standard of care therapies' — i.e. the regulator pre-loaded the exact confound the issuer's Phase 2 design cannot address.

candidate.name: atm_drip_has_no_clearing_print
candidate.one_line: A 'revisit after the raise clears' plan is unexecutable when the issuer's authorized capacity is an ATM rather than a marketed deal — an ATM distributes continuously and never prints a 424B5 clearing event.
candidate.fires_on: Thesis defers entry to a post-financing re-entry AND the issuer's disclosed capacity is an Open Market Sale Agreement / ATM (not a shelf takedown, registered direct, or PIPE). Correct watch plane becomes the sequential 10-Q/10-K share-count series, not S-3/424B5/8-K.
candidate.evidence_here: PROK: brief recommends arming an S-3/424B5/8-K watch and revisiting 'after the raise clears'; actual capacity is a $200M Open Market Sale Agreement with Jefferies (2025-07-14) off S-3 333-275701 — 48% of the $414M cap, distributable with no discrete filing trigger. The watch as specified would never fire while the dilution completed.

candidate.name: conditional_rescue_dosing_flattens_dose_response
candidate.one_line: A randomized dose-comparison whose LOW arm allows a protocol-triggered rescue second dose is not a dose comparison — progressors cross into full dosing, mechanically shrinking the between-arm outcome gap and inviting BOTH bull over-read and bear 'no dose response' over-read.
candidate.fires_on: Trial randomizes 1:1 to dose levels AND the lower arm specifies conditional/rescue escalation keyed to a progression threshold (e.g. eGFR decline >=20%, UACR rise >=30%). Any between-arm outcome difference is then a diluted, non-randomized contrast; neither a dose-response claim nor a no-dose-response refutation is licensed without the as-treated crossover count.
candidate.evidence_here: PROK REGEN-007: Group 2 (n=25) patients received a second contralateral rilparencel injection if eGFR fell >=20% or UACR rose >=30% and >=30 mg/g. The red bench computed 'post-slope difference between a full dose and a half dose = 0.4' and inferred regression-to-the-mean; but G2 is a mixed-dose, progression-enriched arm, so the 0.4 is partly a design artifact. The crossover count was not disclosed in any venue read this session.

candidate.name: undiluted_prize_table_overstates_clearance
candidate.one_line: A magic-funding prize table computed on the CURRENT share count while the same brief separately forecasts a 30-60% dilution overstates per-share upside by exactly that factor — the two halves must be multiplied, not reported side by side.
candidate.fires_on: Any court output containing both (a) a fully-funded counterfactual NPV per share on today's count and (b) a bounded forced-dilution estimate, without a table row applying (b) to (a). Auto-check: does the brief's '+50% clearance' price survive division by (1 + dilution)?
candidate.evidence_here: PROK red bench: prize table on 302.3M shares gives $2.08/sh at PoS 40% and concludes 'financing is NOT the binding constraint on upside.' Its own finding #6 forecasts +46-50% share growth. Applying it: $1.43/sh at PoS 40% vs a $1.51 tape — the name is fairly priced at base-rate PoS, and financing IS the binding constraint. The verdict survived; the stated rationale did not.

candidate.name: sbc_currency_reflexivity
candidate.one_line: When a fixed-DOLLAR stock-comp budget funds the growth engine itself, a share-price decline mechanically accelerates dilution — the cost of the next unit of growth rises as the currency falls.
candidate.fires_on: SBC/revenue >7% AND SBC is customer/talent-acquisition (sales-force, surgeon, or engineer conversion) AND stock down >40% from 52w high AND adj-EBITDA is the headline profit metric. Compute shares-issued-per-year = SBC$ / current px and compare to the historical share-count CAGR struck at higher average prices.
candidate.evidence_here: ATEC: SBC $84M annualized (H1'26 $41.8M, XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) = 9.5% of guided revenue vs 3-5% medtech norm; at $9.31 that is 9.0M sh/yr = 5.8% dilution vs the realized 5.0%/yr struck at higher prices (144.15M 2/2025 -> 154.45M 7/2026). Adj EBITDA $140M less SBC = $56M, so 60% of the 'profit inflection' is the dilution engine.

candidate.name: capex_starve_fcf_guide_conflict
candidate.one_line: A back-half-loaded FCF guide whose only achievable lever is cutting the same capex that produces the guided volume growth — the two guides cannot both be met.
candidate.fires_on: H1 FCF negative AND FY FCF guide requires an H2 swing >2x the prior-year H2, AND the capex line is deployment capital directly coupled to the volume metric being guided (instrument sets, rental fleet, store buildout, rigs). Test: back out required H2 capex from the FCF guide and compare to the capex-per-unit-of-volume implied by the growth guide.
candidate.evidence_here: ATEC H1'26 OCF $21.803M - capex $32.021M = -$10.2M; FY26 guide 'at least $20M FCF' needs +$30M in H2 vs H2'25's +$12.5M. Capex IS surgical instrument sets, which are the input to the guided +20% case growth; capex already re-accelerated from $42.5M (FY25) to $32.0M in H1'26 alone.

candidate.name: sbc_delta_vs_level_test
candidate.one_line: Before crediting an SBC-based kill on an adjusted-EBITDA inflection, test whether the DELTA is SBC-driven, not just the LEVEL — recompute EBITDA-minus-SBC for both periods and compare margin expansion.
candidate.fires_on: A bear case asserts 'the profit inflection is stock comp' on a company whose headline metric is adj EBITDA. Test: (adjEBITDA-SBC)/rev current vs prior. If the ex-SBC margin expansion is within ~50bp of the headline expansion, the inflection is real and the SBC critique is a LEVEL/valuation input only. Second leg: track SBC/revenue across 4 years — flat SBC dollars against compounding revenue is a DECLINING-intensity story that reads as a rising-cost story if only the absolute dollars are quoted.
candidate.evidence_here: ATEC Q2'26: headline adj-EBITDA margin +415bp; ex-SBC margin +409bp (8.32% vs 4.23%). SBC add-back grew only $2.5M ($15.624M -> $18.147M) against a $12.5M adj-EBITDA increase. SBC intensity FY23 16.9% -> FY24 12.0% -> FY25 9.6% -> FY26E 9.2% on roughly flat dollars ($81.2M/$73.3M/$73.7M/~$81M). The red bench's 'the entire inflection is SBC' inverted on this test.

candidate.name: confirmatory_evidence_leg_collapse
candidate.one_line: An FDA-agreed streamlined/single-arm registrational design whose stated predicate was a SEPARATE trial serving as 'confirmatory evidence' — where that separate trial subsequently fails — leaving a design agreement whose consideration no longer exists and which the sponsor quietly stops restating.
candidate.fires_on: Sponsor PR announcing a reduced-sample or single-arm pivotal design that cites another ongoing trial as confirmatory/supportive evidence, followed within 12 months by that trial missing its primary endpoint, with NO subsequent company or FDA statement re-affirming the reduced design.
candidate.evidence_here: RZLT 2025-09-02 PR: FDA granted a 16-patient single-arm upLIFT on the basis that 'sunRIZE ... would serve as confirmatory clinical evidence'; sunRIZE missed primary and key secondary on 2025-12-11 (45% vs 40% placebo); the 2026-01-07, 2026-05-12 and 2026-06-02 disclosures never restate the tumor-HI design predicate.

candidate.name: assigned_role_provenance_gap
candidate.one_line: Issuer books backlog from a contractual role it received by ASSIGNMENT rather than won directly, and never verifies the assignor's own standing in the underlying contract.
candidate.fires_on: 8-K/PR announcing material backlog where the operative words are 'assignment of the contractual role previously held by [X]' or 'consent to assignment', AND the issuer is not an original signatory, AND no performance security or counterparty-standing attestation is disclosed within 30 days.
candidate.evidence_here: FTK 8-K 2026-08-19: PREPA 'consented to the assignment of the contractual role previously held by Enchanted Rock, LLC to the Company' on 7/31/26; on 8/14 the Oversight Board revoked approval citing alleged unauthorized use of Enchanted Rock's name and signature. If the assignor's signature was repudiated, the assigned role never validly existed — yet FTK put $400M/10-yr backlog into an investor PR on 8/4. Termination ground (i) was failure to furnish performance security, against $11.0M of total company liquidity (10-Q 6/30/26).

candidate.name: short_report_forced_disclosure_lag
candidate.one_line: Issuer discloses a known material adverse event only after — and on the same day as — a short-seller publication, converting a disclosure-timing choice into a management-integrity datum.
candidate.fires_on: Gap >=2 trading days between a documented adverse trigger date recited in the issuer's own later 8-K and that 8-K's filing date, where the filing date coincides with a third-party short report the issuer's own release acknowledges.
candidate.evidence_here: FTK's 8-K filed 8/18/26 recites the Oversight Board's 8/14/26 revocation vote; the accompanying Ex-99.1 acknowledges 'a firm with an admitted short interest position in the Company published a report.' Four calendar days on a fact retiring ~57% of stated backlog.

candidate.name: public_repudiation_response_lag
candidate.one_line: The adverse fact is PUBLIC (third-party press statement or regulator release) before the issuer addresses it, so the tell is response latency and market inattention — not concealment; benches that grade it as a securities-fraud disclosure lag mis-specify the mechanism and over-penalize.
candidate.fires_on: A named counterparty or regulator publicly repudiates/revokes a contract the issuer has marketed, AND the issuer's first responsive filing is >=5 calendar days later, AND the issuer's own later 8-K recites the public date. Grade as responsiveness + narrative-fragility, NOT as withheld material non-public information.
candidate.evidence_here: ERock Inc. publicly stated on 2026-08-07 that its name/signature were used without authorization; the Oversight Board publicly announced revocation 2026-08-14; FTK first addressed it 2026-08-18 — one business day after PREPA's own 8/17 stop-work directive, but eleven days after the public repudiation. Red bench graded this as a concealment/RP_TAINTED trigger; the facts were public throughout, so the correct reading is response latency plus a market that failed to connect a Puerto Rico regulator release to a Houston oilfield ticker.

candidate.name: related_party_deconcentration_trend
candidate.one_line: Read customer-concentration as a QoQ TRAJECTORY, not a level: a falling related-party share with rising absolute external revenue converts the standard 'captive revenue' kill into evidence of genuine external inflection.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer discloses related-party/major-customer revenue % for both the quarter and the year-to-date period; back out the prior quarter and compute external revenue in dollars for each. Fires when RP% falls >=10pts QoQ AND absolute external revenue rises >=25% QoQ.
candidate.evidence_here: FTK 10-Q 6/30/26: ProFrac 63.8% of 1H26 ($108.0M) but 56.5% of Q2 ($56.1M) -> implied Q1 74.1%; external revenue $18.1M (Q1) -> $43.3M (Q2), +139% QoQ. The red bench cited the 63.8% YTD figure alone and concluded the inflection was captive; the quarterly trajectory says the opposite. Counterweight the same arithmetic surfaces: ex-ProFrac external growth is only +23.8% y/y (1H25 $49.6M -> 1H26 $61.4M).

candidate.name: registry_vs_guidance_completion_divergence
candidate.one_line: Sponsor's guided topline date vs the SAME trial's ClinicalTrials.gov estimated primary-completion date — a recently-updated registry entry that trails guidance by two or more quarters is a dated, primary-source contradiction of the catalyst calendar.
candidate.fires_on: Company PR guides topline to period T; CT.gov record for the identical NCT shows estimated primary completion >= T + 2 quarters, with a last-update-posted date within 90 days (i.e. the sponsor touched the record and did not pull the date in).
candidate.evidence_here: RZLT guided upLIFT topline to 'second half of 2026' on 2026-05-12 and 2026-06-02; NCT06881992, last update posted 2026-08-17, status recruiting, estimated primary completion September 2027 - a 12-month divergence, with observed enrollment velocity (8 patients since 2025-04-16 across 13 sites) corroborating the registry over the guidance.

candidate.name: payables_funded_operating_cash_flow
candidate.one_line: Operating cash flow held positive entirely by a step-change in accounts-payable build, scaled to revenue — a working-capital stretch masquerading as cash conversion.
candidate.fires_on: Cash-flow-statement change-in-AP divided by period revenue exceeds ~2x the prior-year same-period ratio AND OCF excluding the AP change is negative while OCF including it is positive. Requires the CF-statement organic change, not the balance-sheet delta, so acquired balances are excluded.
candidate.evidence_here: CDNL H1'26 (10-Q acc. 0001193125-26-345109, R8): OCF +$21,995,424 with change-in-AP +$39,648,363 = 10.1% of $394.4M revenue, vs +$7,052,718 = 3.8% of revenue in H1'25. OCF ex-AP: -$17.65M in H1'26 vs +$9.27M in H1'25. Simultaneously the contract-asset build was FLAT on a scaled basis (8.3% vs 7.6% of revenue), so the conventional percentage-of-completion unbilled-receivable detector does NOT fire — the stretch is on the supplier side, and the standard tell misses it.

candidate.name: aspirational_guide_cut_vs_achieved_baseline
candidate.one_line: A 'guidance cut' whose pre-cut number was an aspiration the issuer never actually achieved — the cut lands at or above the realized multi-year run-rate, so the tape prices damage that never existed.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer lowers a percentage guide (margin, take-rate, yield) while raising the absolute-dollar guide, AND the withdrawn percentage exceeds every reported actual for that metric in the available public history. Confirm by pulling the last two full-year actuals before accepting any bear reconstruction anchored on the withdrawn number.
candidate.evidence_here: CDNL pulled a '>20%' FY26 adj EBITDA margin guide to 16-18% on 2026-08-11 and the stock fell ~26%. But FY2025 actual was 17.9% and FY2024 actual was 17.9% (PR 2026-03-19) — >20% was never printed. Absolute adj EBITDA guidance simultaneously ROSE from ~$136M implied to >$150M at the midpoint on revenue raised $680M->$890M. Both the sell-side narrative and this court's own red brief anchored the required step-up on the withdrawn aspiration and on a single weather-impaired quarter (Q2 12.4%) rather than on the seasonally-matched prior-year half (H2'25 = 17.6%), inflating the required improvement from 0-360bp to a claimed 530-880bp.

candidate.name: levered_stub_fx_and_swap_roll_torque
candidate.one_line: In a levered stub, foreign-currency debt tranches and dated interest-rate-swap expiries move per-share value more than operations do, with zero company news.
candidate.fires_on: Equity/EV < 20% AND a debt tranche denominated in a currency other than the reporting currency AND/OR disclosed swap maturities inside the deleveraging thesis horizon.
candidate.evidence_here: PSFE: EUR478.4M (~$560M) of $2.5B debt vs USD-reported EBITDA -> 10% EURUSD = ~$0.85-1.10/sh (12-16% of the sliver); 1M-SOFR swaps expire 2027-12-31 and 2028-03-31 per the 6-K XBRL, a second interest step-up landing inside the 2027+ payoff window.

candidate.name: incremental_margin_of_a_guidance_raise
candidate.one_line: When an issuer raises revenue guidance and cuts percentage-margin guidance, compute the implied margin on the INCREMENTAL revenue — if it is far below both the blended guide and the acquirer's stated acquisition margins, the cut is being borne by the organic base and 'mix dilution' is a false defence.
candidate.fires_on: (new_rev_mid x new_margin_mid) - (old_rev_mid x old_margin_floor), divided by (new_rev_mid - old_rev_mid). Fires when that incremental margin is below the low end of the new blended guide AND the issuer has publicly guided its acquired entities at or above the blended rate. Cross-check against the issuer's own prior-year margin through a comparable acquisition wave.
candidate.evidence_here: CDNL raised FY26 revenue $665-678M to $880-900M while cutting margin from '20%+' to 16-18%. Incremental: +$218.5M revenue for +$6.5 to +27.7M adj EBITDA = 3.0-12.7% incremental margin (~7.8% at midpoints), versus Allied guided at 20.3% and ALGC 'much, much higher'. Solving for the legacy base gives ~$107-112M on $671.5M = ~16.4% vs 20%+, a ~360bp organic cut. The mix-dilution defence is further refuted by the issuer's own history: FY2024 17.9% -> FY2025 17.9% on +45% acquisition-fuelled revenue.

candidate.name: post_combination_comp_addback_in_adjusted_fcf
candidate.one_line: People-business roll-up reports positive 'adjusted free cash flow' by adding back cash retention/earnout payments to the principals of acquired firms, so the metric excludes the actual cost of the assets bought.
candidate.fires_on: Non-GAAP FCF reconciliation whose bridge from OCF contains a 'post-combination compensation', 'deferred acquisition consideration', or 'seller retention payment' add-back exceeding 25% of reported adjusted FCF, AND a balance-sheet obligation for it that grows period-over-period; escalate when reported OCF is negative while adjusted FCF is positive.
candidate.evidence_here: PPHC H1'26: OCF -$9.1M -> AFCF +$4.1M with a $9.6M 'prepaid post-combination expense' add-back (H1'25: $10.3M on -$0.3M OCF). Obligation grew $8.3M -> $15.6M in six months alongside three 2026 deals; simultaneously paid a $7.0M dividend. Compounds with contingent consideration $13.0M -> $16.7M excluded from the 'net debt $5.2M' figure.

candidate.name: guided_h2_residual_margin
candidate.one_line: Back out the implied H2 (or Q4) EBITDA margin from a raised full-year guide minus actual H1 — a 'raise' can embed a sharp second-half step-down that the headline hides.
candidate.fires_on: FY guided EBITDA minus reported H1 EBITDA implies a residual-period margin more than 800bps below the just-reported quarter's margin, while the release is titled as an upgrade.

candidate.name: best_and_final_ceiling_inversion
candidate.one_line: A withdrawn takeover whose price was declared 'best and final' sets a revealed CEILING on that bidder, not a floor under the stock — post-break M&A branches that treat the failed price as a support level are directionally inverted.
candidate.fires_on: Prior offer declared best-and-final, minimum-acceptance condition failed, offer withdrawn, and a valuation tree assigns >=20% probability to a re-offer at or above the failed price without a NEW named bidder or materially improved fundamentals.
candidate.evidence_here: Innosera raised 233->250 'best and final', failed minimum acceptance, withdrew 5-Nov-2025; BAVA FY26 revenue since guided ~-9% YoY with only DKK 800m of 2027 preparedness revenue secured. Desk tree used 250 as a 'reservation-price floor'.

candidate.name: seasonal_h2_residual_control
candidate.one_line: Before calling a guided second-half margin step-down a collapse, compute the SAME residual for the prior year from audited actuals — semiannual reporters with H2-loaded R&D/launch spend show a stable, recurring H2 margin trough.
candidate.fires_on: An implied residual-period margin is used as a bear datum without a prior-year same-residual control; fires when prior-year implied H2 margin is within 200bps of the current implied H2 margin.
candidate.evidence_here: BAVA H2-2025 implied EBITDA-before-special 771 on 3,246 = 23.8% (FY25 1,732 ex-PRV minus H1 961); H2-2026 implied 620 on 2,608 = 23.8%. Red graded a recurring seasonal trough as a guided collapse and called it FATAL.

candidate.name: forward_book_disclosure_lag
candidate.one_line: Contracted-revenue disclosures for year T+1 are systematically thin at the mid-year print because government/institutional orders book on a rolling ~2-quarter lead; comparing T+1-secured against T-secured measures the calendar, not demand.
candidate.fires_on: A bear case cites 'only X secured for next year vs Y for this year' from a mid-year report, without the prior-year mid-year disclosure of the same forward metric as a control.
candidate.evidence_here: BAVA Aug-2026: 2,300m secured 2026 vs 800m secured 2027. Aug-2025 report quantified only current-year ('approximately DKK 3,100 million in contracts ... in 2025') and gave no 2026 figure — yet 2026 PP landed at ~2,500m with 2,300m secured.

candidate.name: fx_band_indexation_carry_reversal
candidate.one_line: When an EM central bank re-indexes its FX crawl/band from a fixed sub-inflation crawl to an inflation-linked path, the real-appreciation carry that drove the ADR complex's rerating is switched off, and IAS-29 constant-currency reporters take the full drag in USD while their local-currency financials still look like they are improving.
candidate.fires_on: Central bank replaces a pre-set nominal crawl (e.g. 1%/mo) with a band indexed to realized inflation (~2.5%/mo), on an issuer reporting under IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting with a USD-listed ADR; symptom is a large ADR drawdown that local-currency operating metrics appear to refute.
candidate.evidence_here: SUPV ADR -41.7% off 52w high while 2Q26 retail 90dpd fell 8.6%->7.9%, NPL 5.5% (210bps below industry), NIM +253bps QoQ. Peso -13.15% YoY; BCRA swapped the 1%/mo crawl for an inflation-indexed band, peso through 1,490/USD. The brief read the drawdown as a credit-narrative artifact and selected a credit refuting-metric; the actual pricing channel is the removal of real-FX carry, which no local-currency asset-quality metric can refute. Diagnostic: a bench that picks a refuting metric denominated in the reporting currency cannot falsify a discount-rate/FX-regime cause.

candidate.name: incentive_fee_holiday_coverage_illusion
candidate.one_line: An externally-managed vehicle's dividend/NII coverage improves because realized credit losses impair the adviser's total-return incentive-fee hurdle, so the coverage metric and the credit-quality claim are the same variable with opposite signs.
candidate.fires_on: Sequential or YoY NII-per-share improvement where the incentive-fee line is zero or negative in the current period and materially positive in the comparison period, AND cumulative realized losses over the lookback window exceed the fee hurdle. Test: re-add the comparison-period incentive fee and recompute coverage; if it falls below ~1.1x, the headline coverage is loss-funded.
candidate.evidence_here: RWAY Q2'26 10-Q statement of operations: incentive fees $(199)k vs $3,523k in Q2'25, a $3.7M swing on $18.2M of NII; normalized coverage 1.04x vs the marketed 1.30x, while the company simultaneously marketed a risk-rating improvement to 2.34 from 2.67.

candidate.name: adviser_side_payment_to_close
candidate.one_line: An external adviser pays its own cash to the seller's holders to get an acquisition closed — a revealed-preference measurement that the deal's value accrues to the fee base, not the shareholders.
candidate.fires_on: Merger 8-K discloses consideration 'contributed by the investment adviser' or 'separate from the purchase price'; size the conflict as adviser outlay vs annualized incremental base fee on acquired gross assets (payback years).
candidate.evidence_here: RWAY 8-K 2026-04-07: adviser 'contributed $9.0 million in cash as consideration to the stockholders of SWK separate from' the $249.0M price, acquiring ~$240M of permanent fee base; shareholders bore the $8.1M transaction cost ($0.22/sh NAV) and leverage moving 0.98x -> 1.36x.

candidate.name: acquired_book_blend_dilution_arithmetic_check
candidate.one_line: When a vehicle reports an improved portfolio-quality average right after absorbing an acquired book, solve the weighted-average decomposition on disclosed weights before accepting OR rejecting the improvement — both benches routinely assert a legacy figure that the disclosed weights cannot produce.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer reports a blended weighted-average quality/rating/yield metric for the first period including an acquisition, without a legacy-vs-acquired split. Compute L = (blend - w*S)/(1-w) across the full plausible range of S; if no value of S in [best, blend] produces the asserted legacy figure, the assertion is arithmetically impossible regardless of which bench made it.

candidate.name: settlement_credit_in_operating_income_base_effect

candidate.name: backlog_conversion_window_restatement_artifact
candidate.one_line: A bear case restates a company's normal seasonal concentration as an impossible share of a longer conversion window ('one quarter must absorb 40-49% of a full year of contracted conversion'), producing an alarming ratio that is arithmetically identical to what the issuer does every year.
candidate.fires_on: Any finding that divides a single-period requirement by a multi-period disclosed conversion estimate (RPO %-over-12-months, backlog burn rate, contracted-revenue schedule) WITHOUT first testing the issuer's own historical per-quarter distribution of that same window. Fires hardest on fiscal-Q4-loaded hardware/EPC/integrator businesses, where 40-46% of annual revenue in the closing quarter is the baseline, not the outlier. The tell: the finding presents the ratio as self-evidently impossible and cites no seasonality series.
candidate.evidence_here: FLNC red bench nominated as STRONGEST SINGLE KILL that Q4 FY26's required $1.31-1.51B is '39-49% of a full year of contracted RPO conversion' -- while the same bench's own Finding 1 had already established Q4 FY24 = 2.54x Q3 and 45.5% of FY, and FY25 Q4 = 43.5% of FY. A book converting 48-53% in twelve months is FRONT-LOADED by construction (a flat four-year book converts 25%), so a Q4-heavy issuer drawing 40-49% of that window in its seasonal peak quarter is the base case, not the tail. The bench caught the thesis's base-effect trick and then committed the mirror-image one in its own headline finding.

candidate.name: coupon_anchor_no_nav_closure

The cause-check and the valuation claim were mutually exclusive and no one checked.

candidate.name: price_invariant_reflexive_buyin_strike
candidate.one_line: A contractual buy-in whose strike is the issuer's OWN trading multiple, settled in the issuer's OWN stock, transfers a fixed FRACTION of the company regardless of share price — drawdowns give zero relief, and the acquired unit's growth enlarges the transfer.

Every bull datum (UFEC +37%, PW assets >$21B, record $2.8B quarterly subscriptions) raises SPW ANI and therefore the transferred fraction.

candidate.name: finance_lease_omission_in_funded_debt

candidate.name: guidance_raise_below_the_beat

candidate.name: single_asset_annuity_treadmill
candidate.one_line: A royalty/annuity book marketed on asset COUNT whose revenue is a rotating series of single-mine annuities, each individually wasting, masking a halving residual portfolio.

candidate.name: guidance_delta_vs_wrong_baseline

candidate.name: unit_economics_plausibility_backtest_on_decomposition

candidate.name: administrative_scarcity_offswitch
candidate.one_line: A commodity margin priced as 'structural physical scarcity' is materially sourced from a government EXPORT BAN with a publicly stated lift condition — a stroke-of-the-pen reversal that the tape models as a multi-year rebuild.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer margin is levered to a supply shortfall where >=25% of the missing volume is withheld by decree (export ban, quota, sanction waiver) rather than destroyed capacity, AND the withholding authority has publicly named a condition for lifting it.
candidate.evidence_here: Record HO crack ~$105 attributed to Russian refining destruction; primary reporting shows Russia's diesel+gasoline EXPORT BAN (extended to end-Jan-2027) is a separate, additive withholding, with Moscow stating it will end 'when the market recovers.' Physical outages are month-scale CDU/ADU repairs (Ryazan ~1mo, Novokuybyshevsk ADU), not multi-year. Blue's persistence premise conflates the two.

candidate.name: insurance_recovery_inflated_fcf
candidate.one_line: Operating cash flow and headline EPS at a post-catastrophe issuer are inflated by terminating insurance installments and LCM reversals, exactly when a bull case wants to annualize spot FCF.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer had a major property loss in the prior 24 months AND reports a 'gain on insurance recoveries' line AND an inventory LCM reversal in the same period; test = (OCF - insurance proceeds - LCM effect) / OCF < 0.75 while the asset is already restored to full operations (i.e. the stream terminates).
candidate.evidence_here: PBF H1-26: OCF $1,265.1M includes $356.5M insurance gain (5th installment; $1.25B cumulative) and net income includes a $313.0M non-cash LCM reversal, while Martinez 'returned to full operations in May 2026' — 45% of H1 FCF is non-recurring and the stream is ending.

adjudication_note: pair w/ insurance_gain_ocf_double_subtraction: run the check, then audit for double-counting vs the reconciliation

candidate.name: regulatory_refund_in_adjusted_earnings
candidate.one_line: Adjusted EBITDA/EPS inflated by a one-time regulatory refund or exemption credit that management itself declines to call operating income.
candidate.fires_on: A non-GAAP reconciliation line naming a government exemption, waiver, credit refund, or compliance-obligation reversal that ADDS to adjusted EBITDA, AND the issuer publishes an ex-item alternative figure, AND a transcript quote characterizes it as a return of prior-period cash.
candidate.evidence_here: DK Q2-26 8-K/A: +$148.6M 'small refinery exemption RVO short' inside $638.7M adj EBITDA; company's own ex-RVO figures $3.64/sh and $490.1M; CFO: 'It's the cash that we have already invested and is being returned to us.' Headline '+148% beat vs $2.21' drove a 52w-high re-rate.

candidate.name: unrealized_compliance_liability_addback

candidate.fires_on: Non-GAAP reconciliation contains 'unrealized change in fair value of [RIN/carbon/REC/emissions] obligation' as a positive add-back while the underlying credit price is in an uptrend.
candidate.evidence_here: DK added back $210.5M of unrealized net RINs obligation fair-value change (35% of headline adj EBITDA) against a 2025 RVO the CFO sized at $468.4M at ~$1/gal RINs; the obligation settles in cash unless RIN prices retrace.

candidate.name: insurance_gain_ocf_double_subtraction
candidate.one_line: An analyst adjusting OCF for 'non-recurring insurance' subtracts an income-statement GAIN that the cash-flow statement already reconciled out — removing cash that was never in operating activities.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer reports a 'gain on insurance recoveries' in operating income AND a cash-flow statement showing that gain as a negative reconciling item, with actual proceeds split across operating and investing; test = does the adjustment subtract the GAIN (income-statement) or the operating-classified PROCEEDS (cash-flow)? Pair with a check that deferred turnaround expenditures are included in capex.
candidate.evidence_here: PBF H1-26: red subtracted the full $356.5M gain from $1,265.1M OCF, but the 10-Q shows '(356.5)' as an operating add-back, $111.3M operating proceeds and $245.2M in INVESTING reimbursing excluded Martinez rebuild capex; red separately omitted $242.4M of deferred turnaround expenditures from capex. Two errors nearly cancelled, producing a right answer from a wrong mechanism.

adjudication_note: counter-detector of insurance_recovery_inflated_fcf (PBF red error caught by blue)

candidate.name: stale_satellite_preflight_as_current_evidence

candidate.fires_on: Any satellite/thermal/storage detector output whose latest_date is >120 days before the decision date, OR whose per-site series start dates differ by >6 months while trends are compared across sites.
candidate.evidence_here: PBF oil_storage latest_date 2025-10-16/2025-10-20 cited to corroborate 2026 crack capture; plant_thermal series start 2023-11 (Delaware), 2025-02 (Martinez), 2025-08 (Chalmette) yet the -2.24 vs +0.05 C/yr trends were compared directly to conclude 'capture is one-region'.

candidate.name: one_sided_addback_scrub
candidate.one_line: An analyst 'cleans' adjusted EBITDA by disallowing the add-backs that flatter the issuer while silently accepting the issuer's own subtractions, producing a base no consistent method yields.
candidate.fires_on: A bench-computed 'clean EBITDA' equals headline adj EBITDA minus only the POSITIVE reconciling lines, while the same reconciliation contains material NEGATIVE lines (inventory gains, unrealized hedging gains, intercompany charges) left untouched. Test: does the bench's number reconcile to GAAP EBITDA by any consistent rule?
candidate.evidence_here: Red computed DK clean Q2-26 EBITDA $279.6M = 638.7 - 148.6 - 210.5, ignoring -$157.3M other inventory impact and -$23.1M unrealized hedging gains that DK itself removed. Consistent bases: $638.7M (DK adj), $433.9M (GAAP, all marks in), $460.0M (symmetric scrub). Refining per-bbl error: $12.60 claimed vs $19.36-19.72 on any consistent basis.

candidate.name: tape_above_consensus_target_at_52w_high

candidate.fires_on: spot > mean 12m PT across >=8 analysts AND >=80% of individual targets <= spot AND price within 10% of the 52w high. Gates ENTRY, not the thesis; a divergence with a named mechanism can still clear it.
candidate.evidence_here: DK $72.16 vs mean PT $64.33 (12 analysts, high $85 low $45); UBS Neutral $52, Mizuho $66, GS $83 - only 1 of 12 above spot. Neither bench pulled this; it decided the entry gate where the accounting argument did not.

candidate.name: margin_laundering_via_services_acquisition
candidate.one_line: A hardware/robotics issuer with structurally negative product gross margin acquires a low-margin human-labor services business, inverting the blended cost-of-revenue ratio below 100% without any improvement in the core unit's economics.
candidate.fires_on: Cost-of-revenue/revenue ratio crosses below 100% in the SAME quarter or the quarter after an Item 2.01 acquisition closes, while no segment disclosure separates the acquired line; blended gross margin lands in the single digits typical of labor services rather than the target margin of the product story.
candidate.evidence_here: KSCP cost/revenue ran 116-160% FY2021-25 (XBRL CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold/RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax); Event Risk, LLC closed 2026-02-27 (8-K/A Item 2.01, acc. 0001104659-26-062519); Q1'26 92.3% and Q2'26 92.6% - the first sub-100% quarters in company history, at ~7.4% blended gross margin, with revenue 2,749k -> 9,024k YoY and no ASR-vs-services segment split.

candidate.name: acquiree_contribution_residual_split
candidate.one_line: Uses the ASC 805 'revenue and earnings of the acquiree since acquisition date' disclosure to arithmetically back out the LEGACY segment's standalone unit economics when the issuer reports a single blended segment.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer closes a material acquisition, collapses to (or remains) a single reportable segment, and headline growth is attributed to the combined line; the 805 note then permits legacy = consolidated minus acquiree for revenue, gross margin and net income.
candidate.evidence_here: KSCP H1'26 consolidated revenue $15,040k / gross profit $1,129k / net loss -$24,410k; 10-Q business-combination note discloses KSF contributed revenue $9.2M, gross margin $2.0M, net income +$0.2M; residual legacy = $5,840k revenue, -$871k gross profit (114.9% cost ratio), +3% YoY - i.e. the robot business is still gross-margin-negative and flat while the headline reads +228%.

candidate.name: pro_forma_perimeter_growth_check
candidate.one_line: Compares the ASC 805 pro-forma prior-period combined revenue and net loss against the current actual, converting a perimeter-inflated growth headline into like-for-like growth and like-for-like loss trajectory.
candidate.fires_on: Any period whose YoY revenue growth exceeds ~50% and which contains an acquisition closing; compare actual current vs pro-forma prior.
candidate.evidence_here: KSCP headline H1 revenue +165% ($5,666k -> $15,040k); pro forma H1'25 combined revenue $13,397k makes it +12.3%, while pro forma H1'25 combined net loss -$14,540k vs actual H1'26 -$24,410k shows the loss widened 68% on an identical perimeter.

candidate.name: sponsor_carry_distribution_ebitda_addback
candidate.one_line: In Up-C/sponsor-controlled post-IPO issuers, cash carry distributions from the PARENT entity to management on legacy profits interests are expensed at the issuer and then added back to Adjusted EBITDA as 'stock-based and other non-cash compensation' — making the add-back recur with, and only with, sponsor monetization.
candidate.fires_on: SBC/comp add-back is a large share of Adjusted EBITDA (>25%) AND disclosed unrecognized grant-date compensation is far smaller than the quarterly expense AND the equity note references distributions by 'the Parent Entities' or sponsor vehicles to interest holders.
candidate.evidence_here: LGN Q2-26: $73.9M 'stock-based and other non-cash compensation' add-back = 48% of $154.6M adj EBITDA; Time Interests expense $52.0M in the quarter vs only $24.6M TOTAL unrecognized cost over 3.2 years; 10-Q states 'the Parent Entities distributed $34.7 million and $45.8 million' to Time Interests holders, included in compensation expense. Structurally couples the SBC-run-off bull case to the sponsor-overhang bear case: they cannot both resolve favorably.

adjudication_note: AMENDED: flag the add-back but VERIFY WHO SETTLES before capitalizing as issuer cost (LGN: aggregators settle, barred from issuer cash - red capitalized wrongly)

candidate.name: tra_accretes_on_exchange_ev_basis_error
candidate.one_line: In Up-C issuers with a Tax Receivable Agreement, valuing on a FULLY-EXCHANGED share count while using TODAY'S TRA liability systematically understates EV — each Class B exchange mechanically creates new TRA cash obligation.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer has a TRA liability on the balance sheet AND unexchanged OpCo/Class B units outstanding AND an analysis uses fully-diluted/fully-exchanged shares in the equity value.
candidate.evidence_here: LGN TRA rose $207.4M -> $342.7M in 6 months, of which $143.6M is exchange-driven ($133.8M from the 4/9/26 secondary alone) for ~10.3M units exchanged (~$13M per 1M units). 31.2M Class B remain: ~$400M of unbooked EV. Brief's $6.56B fully-exchanged EV understates by ~6%.

candidate.name: aggregator_settled_profits_interest_pushdown
candidate.one_line: In sponsor-controlled Up-C issuers, profits-interest compensation SETTLED BY THE PARENT'S management aggregator — expensed at the issuer with an offsetting capital contribution and no issuer cash or Class A dilution — is a legitimate EBITDA add-back, and treating it as a real cost is a bear-side basis error symmetric to the bull-side add-back error.
candidate.fires_on: Equity note states a parent/aggregator vehicle is 'solely responsible for settling these awards' AND the offsetting entry is 'capital contributions from' that vehicle AND quarterly expense far exceeds disclosed unrecognized grant-date cost (fair-value remeasurement, not amortization).
candidate.evidence_here: LGN Note 11: Management Aggregators solely responsible and cannot direct Legence Holdings to settle; Time Interests remeasured at fair value each period with changes recognized as capital contributions; $52.0M Q2 expense vs only $24.6M total unrecognized cost over 3.2 years. Corollary: because the awards are MARKED TO THE SHARE PRICE, a 51% drawdown mechanically collapses the expense next quarter — so annualizing a peak-price quarter overstates run-rate comp.

adjudication_note: counter-detector of sponsor_carry_distribution_ebitda_addback; primary-verified at LGN adjudication

candidate.name: zero_incremental_margin_revenue_rolloff
candidate.one_line: When a licensee loses a large licensed-brand revenue stream, the EBITDA damage is set by the stream's INCREMENTAL gross margin, not its revenue share — a roll-off can cut 10% of sales while gross profit dollars stay flat, making revenue-cliff headlines a mispricing rather than an impairment.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer guides a named multi-hundred-million revenue loss from expiring licenses AND reports gross profit DOLLARS flat-to-up YoY over two or more consecutive quarters once one-time COGS credits are stripped; compute (delta GP / delta revenue) as the incremental margin of the exiting business and compare to the reported blended margin.
candidate.evidence_here: GIII Q2 FY27: revenue -$59.2M, gross profit -$0.09M => 0.15% incremental GM; H1 ex-$102.8M IEEPA COGS credit: revenue -$106.8M, GP -$1.7M => 1.6%. Red bench read the same flat GP dollars as bearish ('zero growth'), inverting the sign. Guard: the FY26-vs-FY25 read implies ~34% incremental, so the metric must be computed on at least two vintages before it is load-bearing.

adjudication_note: accepted at GIII adjudication 2026-09-03; zero_incremental_margin two-vintage guard validated live (FY26 vintage tariff-contaminated, caught at primary)

candidate.name: price_war_precedes_pivotal

candidate.fires_on: Issuer's registry-confirmed primary completion date postdates a first-mover's approval AND the first mover launches at >70% discount to the incumbent modality's price; issuer's own PRs still cite pre-collapse pricing assumptions.
candidate.evidence_here: GPCR ACCOMPLISH-1 primary completion Sept-2028 (NCT07654361) vs orforglipron approval 2026-04-01 at $149-299/mo self-pay and $25/mo commercial; street PT $110.91 vs tape $47.34.

candidate.name: placebo_adjusted_vs_absolute_estimand_swap
candidate.one_line: Sponsor headlines a placebo-adjusted efficacy delta while approved competitors headline absolute mean change, inflating the apparent gap.
candidate.fires_on: PR headline metric contains 'placebo-adjusted' AND the cited competitor benchmark is an absolute mean; recompute absolute = headline + placebo arm change.
candidate.evidence_here: GPCR 16.3% placebo-adjusted @44wk (placebo +1.1% -> ~15.2% absolute) vs ATTAIN-1 12.4% absolute @72wk and OASIS-4 13.6% @64wk; secondary media already reprinted 14.7% as absolute.

candidate.name: titration_dose_price_mistaken_for_category_price
candidate.one_line: An analyst prices a drug category off the advertised starting-dose self-pay price when the clinically effective maintenance dose costs multiples more, understating peak revenue per patient.
candidate.fires_on: A competitive-pricing kill cites a '$X starting at' figure; check the payer/self-pay schedule for the maintenance-dose price and use that in peak-sales math.
candidate.evidence_here: Red modeled the oral GLP-1 category at $1,800/yr from orforglipron's $149/mo starting price; the maintenance schedule runs to $349/mo ($4,188/yr), which flips the valuation kill.

candidate.name: private_parent_holds_the_loved_brand
candidate.one_line: A consumer-love or virality signal names a brand whose legal owner is a PRIVATE parent or affiliate, while the tradeable ticker is a listed subsidiary that books none of it.
candidate.fires_on: Any thesis sourced from product affection/heat where (a) the group has a private holding company or unlisted sibling, and (b) the specific SKU's manufacturer-of-record on the issuer's own product page or press release is NOT the listed entity. Resolve the SKU to its manufacturer-of-record BEFORE valuing the listed vehicle.
candidate.evidence_here: Suntory All-Free / のんある気分 / のんある酒場 / まるで梅酒なノンアルコール are all products of サントリー株式会社 (private Suntory Holdings' alcohol arm), per suntory.co.jp's own product FAQ and new-product releases. 2587.T (Suntory Beverage & Food) sells zero NA-beer SKUs, yet was courted as the expression of an NA-substitution thesis. The ~¥5.0bn 2026 NA marketing budget is private-entity spend.

candidate.name: esg_ratio_target_read_as_growth_target
candidate.one_line: A sustainability-report MIX-RATIO target is cited as evidence of a growth/substitution thesis, but the ratio is satisfiable by shrinking the denominator — often the issuer's highest-margin volume.
candidate.fires_on: A load-bearing thesis claim cites an issuer target expressed as 'X% composition ratio by YEAR' sourced from a sustainability/ESG page rather than financial guidance, with no revenue or margin attached. Check: is the denominator the issuer's premium product? Does hitting the ratio require the numerator to grow, or merely the denominator to fall?
candidate.evidence_here: Asahi Group's 'achieve a 20% sales composition ratio of non and low-alcohol adult beverages to major alcohol beverage products by 2030' (scope: beer-type + RTD + NA adult) sits on the sustainability/alcohol page with no revenue or profit attached. The denominator is liquor-taxed premium beer; Asahi hits 20% fastest by LOSING its highest-ASP volume, making the 'substitution economics' margin-dilutive cannibalisation rather than growth. The court brief treated this ESG target as the direct-substitution P&L leg.

candidate.name: excise_convergence_step_corrupts_substitution_signal
candidate.one_line: A dated excise-tax convergence step inverts relative shelf pricing between substitute categories AND injects 2-3 quarters of pre-buy/destock into the monthly volume series, making any substitution-trend read uninterpretable exactly when the thesis needs it.
candidate.fires_on: Issuer whose thesis rests on category-mix migration, where a statutory rate change with a known effective date lands within 2 quarters of the observation window; check the direction of the rate change against the thesis direction.
candidate.evidence_here: Japan liquor-tax final unification 2026-10-01: beer duty -14.4% (63.35->54.25 yen/350ml), happoshu/new-genre +15.5% to converge. Makes full-strength beer relatively CHEAPER, anti-substitution, and distorts Q3/Q4 Japanese beer shipment prints that the thesis named as its native watch plane.

candidate.name: esg_target_horizon_slip
candidate.one_line: A public non-financial mix/volume target is quietly re-dated to a later horizon (2025 -> 2030) in current materials without any miss disclosure, and the last disclosed interim level is far below the original glidepath.
candidate.fires_on: Diff the target year and threshold for the same named KPI across the issuer's own materials over time; FIRE when the year moves later, the threshold is unchanged or the category definition broadens, and no reconciliation to the original deadline is published.
candidate.evidence_here: Asahi Smart Drinking: '0-3.5% ABV + non-alcohol = 20% of Japan volume by 2025' (Dec 2020, from 6%); last disclosed interim 12.1% at H1-2024; current framing is '20% or more by 2030' with the category broadened to include RTD and adult soft drinks. No 2025 outturn published. The slip is the finding: the issuer's own instrument says the trend runs at ~half plan.

adjudication_note: REJECTED at NA-court adjudication: red compared SKU-line-up KPI vs sales KPI (blue audit) - the slip is a denominator-swap artifact, not evidence; see accepted counter-detector target_denominator_swap_false_slip

candidate.name: untaxed_substitute_survives_excise_step
candidate.one_line: When an excise convergence step is used to argue a substitution thesis is dead, check whether the substitute is inside the tax base at all — an untaxed substitute is excluded from both the price move AND the pre-buy/destock distortion, so its disclosure series stays clean while the taxed categories go unreadable.
candidate.fires_on: Any excise/duty step change cited as evidence against (or for) a category-migration thesis; test membership of the thesis category in the statutory tax base, and test whether the issuer discloses that category as a separate line in its monthly/quarterly volume series.
candidate.evidence_here: Japan liquor tax unification 2026-10-01: Kirin's 2026-05-20 price-revision notice raises happoshu, new-genre AND RTD, cuts beer, and explicitly excludes non-alcoholic beverages. Asahi's monthly disclosure prints non-alcohol (Dry Zero 105% YoY, May 2026) as its own line. Red bench claimed the NA series would be uninterpretable through Q2-2027; it is not distorted at all.

candidate.name: target_denominator_swap_false_slip
candidate.one_line: An apparent 'quietly re-dated / missed target' finding is an artifact when the two targets being compared have different denominators (line-up/SKU count vs sales vs volume) or different thresholds — the issuer never restated anything, the analyst compared two coexisting KPIs.
candidate.fires_on: Before filing a target-slip finding, pin BOTH targets' {metric, denominator, threshold, horizon, announcement date}; kill the finding if the later target predates the earlier deadline or measures a different base.
candidate.evidence_here: Asahi: Dec-2020 Smart Drinking pledge = <=3.5% ABV as 20% of the LINE-UP by 2025; group SALES targets = 15% by 2025 and 20% by 2030, the latter public by May 2022. Red filed a '2025->2030 silent slip, running at half plan'; against the correct 15% sales denominator, 12.1% at H1-2024 is ~81% of plan and nothing was re-dated.

candidate.name: cannibalisation_adjusted_supplier_tam
candidate.one_line: A supplier-TAM estimate for a new product category is inflated when it multiplies the new category's volume by its input dose without netting the input dose already carried by the volume the new category displaces.
candidate.fires_on: Any picks-and-shovels thesis where the end category is a SUBSTITUTE for an existing category served by the same supplier (NA beer vs beer, plant milk vs dairy, EV vs ICE aftermarket, e-cig vs tobacco flavour). Test: does the sponsor's TAM arithmetic contain a displacement term? If new_category_volume x dose appears with no (dose_new - dose_displaced) adjustment, FIRE.
candidate.evidence_here: GIVN NA-beer thesis sized the flavour pool as NA hectolitres x EUR/hL dose (EUR 40-390m). IWSR's own series shows no-alcohol +8% against beer overall -1% (theiwsr.com) - the category is a mix shift inside a shrinking denominator, and every displaced full-strength litre already carried hop and flavour spend. candidate.name: drawdown_cause_attribution
